text:
mike: quick q — running into flaky failures when our client hits 429s during streaming + auth refresh. what's the current recommended strategy for retries + idempotency keys?

anna: short answer: distinguish 429 vs 5xx, and be careful with streaming resume vs retrying whole request. idempotency keys for non-idempotent endpoints, always safe to attach for mutating calls. for streaming reads, prefer resumable cursor tokens.

mike: concrete example: node client starts stream with bearer token that expires mid-stream (401), then we get 429 on reconnect. should client auto-retry? code: ```js
// pseudo
await fetchStream(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } })
.on('data', ... )
.on('error', err => { /* 429 or 401 */ })
```

anna: if 401 from expired token -> refresh then resume if possible. if 429: backoff + respect Retry-After if present. do NOT retry indefinitely for streaming unless you have a resume token.

jen: language question — in Go, how should context cancellation interact with retries? if ctx.Done(), we bail immediately, but should we still do one graceful reconnect attempt?

kevin: for Go client: respect ctx for external cancellation. internally you can do a single quick retry (100-200ms) for transient 5xx/429 if ctx still active. don't spin. example pattern: ```go
for attempt := 0; attempt < max; attempt++ {
  select { case <-ctx.Done(): return ctx.Err() default: }
  // call
  if shouldRetry(resp) { sleep(backoff(attempt)) ; continue }
  break
}
```

mike: what about jitter? we've seen synchronized retries causing spikes.

anna: always use full-jitter or equal-jitter. our recommended backoff: base=200ms, max=10s, full-jitter: sleep = rand(0, min(max, base*2^attempt)). this smooths thundering herds.

kevin: note: for 429 with Retry-After header, honor it exactly (if within a sane bound). if Retry-After is huge, treat as capacity signal and fail fast to caller with guidance to try later.

jen: idempotency keys — what's the expiry window on server side? are they one-time or sticky?

anna: servers keep idempotency state for 24h by default for mutating endpoints. key format: UUID v4 or deterministic HMAC of payload + client-id. include header `Idempotency-Key`. document in SDKs: generate if caller didn't provide.

mike: streaming resumption tokens — are those stable across model switch / fallback?

anna: resume tokens are only guaranteed for the same model + same checkpoint. if we fall back to smaller model because of capacity, resume might be invalid. fallback policy should favor a full restart with idempotency key for mutation or return a resume-not-supported error for reads.

mike: CI bot shows flake in e2e that matches this flow. ci-bot: build #3421 failed — timeout on streaming test (reconnect after 429). link: https://ci.internal/3421 :sad_panda:

kevin: I'll pick up a small fix — implement full-jitter + honor Retry-After, and add a resume-token validity check before attempting resume.

jen: pinging @anna and @mike for quick review of the PR when ready. also can we add a note in the SDK README about auth token refresh interaction? tiny doc patch will help support.

mike: thanks — PR coming in a bit. rough plan:
- add env var to toggle aggressive retries for dev testing
- implement full-jitter with base=200ms max=10s
- respect Retry-After and cap to 30s before surfacing error
- generate Idempotency-Key when missing for mutating calls
- for streams: attempt resume only if resume_token && same_model, else fail with recoverable error

anna: sounds good. for the PR title use: "client: resilient retries + resume-token guard" and mention behavioural tests. I'll review quick. :thumbsup:

mike: tagging the test owners @jen and @kevin — will include a small harness to simulate 429 bursts + token expiry.

deploy-bot: FYI — rolling canary in staging with updated client will run at 16:00 UTC if PR merged and green.

mike: cool. thanks all. follow-up: if anyone has objections to the 24h idempotency window or Retry-After cap, speak now or open an issue.

jen: no objections. :eyes:

kevin: lgtm, will start implementation after lunch.

anna: thanks — closing the loop here, but leave thread open for PR comments.
